title: 第一部分 基础训练 TEST 4

sections.title: 阅读理解 A
sections.instruction: 阅读下面语言材料，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
#### **WRITING COMPETITIONS FOR KIDS**

This is the page where you'll find writing competitions for kids! Every competition is different, so be sure to read the guidelines (参考) before taking part in.

* **Write the World (All Countries)**
  * **Notice:** Your writing about the whole world is welcomed. Anything that is meaningful (有意义的) to you can be written.
  * **Deadline (截止日期):** May 14, 2024
  * **Ages:** 11-15

* **Life's Too Good Art and Poetry Competition (US Only)**
  * **Notice:** Only poems about how beautiful life is can be sent to this competition.
  * **Deadline:** September 30, 2024
  * **Ages:** Middle school students

* **JAL World Children's Haiku Competition (All Countries)**
  * **Notice:** Haiku is a Japanese form of poetry. If you want to take part in this competition, be sure that you know haiku clearly and can write it well.
  * **Deadline:** February 29, 2024
  * **Ages:** 15 and under

To find out more about a certain competition, click HERE.

questions.prompt: What do Write the World and JAL World Children's Haiku Competition have in common?
options: A. They accept works from all over the world.
B. They both welcome students over 15.
C. Their deadlines are on the same day.
D. Only students from high school can take part in them.
questions.translation: Write the World 和 JAL World Children's Haiku Competition 有什么共同之处？
questions.explanation: 根据两个比赛标注的 '(All Countries)' 可知，它们都面向全球所有国家的参赛者，即接受来自世界各地的作品。答案为A。

questions.prompt: If Jane likes writing poems about the good side of life, she is very likely to take part in ________.
options: A. Write the World
B. Life's Too Good Art and Poetry Competition
C. JAL World Children's Haiku Competition
D. all of them
questions.translation: 如果简喜欢写关于生活美好一面的诗歌，她很可能会参加________。
questions.explanation: 根据第二个比赛 Notice: 'Only poems about how beautiful life is can be sent to this competition.'（只有关于生活多么美好的诗歌才能发送到该比赛）可知，她很可能参加 Life's Too Good Art and Poetry Competition。答案为B。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
options: A. Adults are not welcomed to take part in the competitions.
B. It is not necessary to read the guidelines.
C. Competitors can write any poems for the last competition.
D. Kids under 10 can take part in Write the World.
questions.translation: 根据文章内容，下列哪项是正确的？
questions.explanation: 标题写明“WRITING COMPETITIONS FOR KIDS”，且三个比赛均限定青少年/中学生，因此成年人不被邀请参加。答案为A。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the passage?
options: A. To introduce some kinds of poems.
B. To share the beauty of life.
C. To encourage all people to write.
D. To call on kids to join the competitions.
questions.translation: 这篇文章的目的是什么？
questions.explanation: 文章介绍了三个面向儿童/青少年的写作比赛信息，旨在号召并吸引孩子们报名参加写作比赛。答案为D。

questions.prompt: Where can the passage be taken from?
options: A. A book.
B. A website.
C. A newspaper.
D. A magazine.
questions.translation: 这篇文章可能出自哪里？
questions.explanation: 文章首句出现'This is the page...'以及末尾出现'click HERE'（点击这里），均为网页的典型特征，因此选网站（A website）。答案为B。

sections.title: 阅读理解 B
sections.instruction: 阅读下面语言材料，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
Haley Evans has always had a special place in her heart for literature. When she was young, she made a family newspaper with her mother. In the third grade, she worked with an organization to collect around 2,000 books for children. So far, she has collected about 8,000 books in all.

This year, the middle school student from the United States made another amazing project. She opened a Free Little Library in Oakland University with her friend Megan MacKenzie.

Haley came up with the idea after reading a piece of news. In Detroit, US, people make Free Little Libraries for kids who don't have enough money to buy books. Little Free Libraries also have themes, such as summer-themed books, holiday-themed books and back-to-school books.

During the interview, she told Simons from *The Oakland Post*, "I like the idea because I never got to read as much when I was a kid. And it really encourages reading, so hopefully kids can grow up with a really large vocabulary and get more interested in reading."

Now, Haley and Megan's Free Little Library is supplied (提供) with children's books, but the girls plan to put in more books for adults soon. Their another two libraries will open next month.

questions.prompt: Haley Evans has collected about ________ books in all.
questions.translation: 海莉·埃文斯总共收集了大约________本书。
questions.explanation: 根据第一段最后一句“So far, she has collected about 8,000 books in all.”可知，一共收集了约8,000本书。答案为C。

questions.prompt: Who opened a Free Little Library in Oakland University?
options: A. Haley.
B. Haley and her mother.
C. Haley and Megan.
D. Haley together with an organization.
questions.translation: 谁在奥克兰大学开办了一座免费小图书馆？
questions.explanation: 根据第二段第二句“She opened a Free Little Library in Oakland University with her friend Megan MacKenzie.”可知，是海莉和她的朋友梅根。答案为C。

questions.prompt: Books in Free Little Libraries are free for ________.
options: A. poor children
B. adults
C. high school students
D. university students
questions.translation: 免费小图书馆里的书是对________免费的。
questions.explanation: 根据第三段第二句“In Detroit, US, people make Free Little Libraries for kids who don't have enough money to buy books.”可知，是为没有足够的钱买书的贫困儿童设立的。答案为A。

questions.prompt: We can infer that Simons is a ________.
options: A. head teacher
B. bookseller
C. reader
D. reporter
questions.translation: 我们可以推断西蒙斯是一名________。
questions.explanation: 根据第四段“During the interview, she told Simons from The Oakland Post...”可知，在接受采访时她告诉来自《奥克兰邮报》的西蒙斯，因此推断西蒙斯是一名记者（reporter）。答案为D。

sections.title: 阅读理解 C
sections.instruction: 阅读下面语言材料，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
José Hernández knew he wanted to be an astronaut at age 10, after watching the Apollo 17 moon landing with his parents on their black-and-white TV in 1972. Now his journey to space has been made into a new film called *A Million Miles Away*. The film is based on (根据) *Reaching for the Stars*, the 2012 book Hernández wrote about his life. Actor Michael Peña acted the role of Hernández in the film and he had a great performance.

Hernández grew up in California. His parents were farm workers who moved from Mexico to the US. They worked long hours in the fields, and Hernández often worked with them. In pursuit (追求) of his dream to become an astronaut, he studied math and science in college.

In 2001, Hernández began working as an engineer at NASA. In 2004, after applying (申请) 12 times, he was finally accepted into NASA's astronaut program. His first trip to space was in 2009 on the STS-128 Discovery mission, which lasted about 14 days. "Words cannot describe how you feel when you get up into space," Hernández once said. "As I was looking down at our Earth, I felt I was the luckiest man on Earth."

With *A Million Miles Away*, Hernández's message for young people with big dreams is that with family, education, and determination (决心), "the sky is not the limit, space is."

questions.prompt: When was José Hernández born?
questions.translation: 何塞·埃尔南德斯是什么时候出生的？
questions.explanation: 根据第一段首句“...knew he wanted to be an astronaut at age 10, after watching the Apollo 17 moon landing... in 1972.”可知，1972年时他10岁，推算出生年份为1972 - 10 = 1962年。答案为A。

questions.prompt: Hernández's parents ________.
options: A. came from California, US
B. were both engineers at NASA
C. worked for a long time in the fields
D. hoped their son would become an astronaut
questions.translation: 埃尔南德斯的父母________。
questions.explanation: 根据第二段第二句“They worked long hours in the fields, and Hernández often worked with them.”可知，他的父母在田里长时间工作。答案为C。

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE about Hernández?
options: A. He stayed in space for about a month on his first mission.
B. He was turned down many times before his first flying.
C. He was considered as the first man to land on the moon.
D. He worked hard at NASA as an astronaut after college.
questions.translation: 关于埃尔南德斯，下列哪项是正确的？
questions.explanation: 根据第三段“after applying (申请) 12 times, he was finally accepted into NASA's astronaut program”可知，他在申请了12次后才被录取，说明在此之前他被拒绝了许多次（turned down many times）。答案为B。

questions.prompt: What does Hernández want to express in the new film?
options: A. His ideas about big dreams.
B. His thankfulness for his parents.
C. Improve your life as early as possible.
D. Studying math and science is interesting.
questions.translation: 埃尔南德斯想在新的电影中表达什么？
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段“...Hernández's message for young people with big dreams is that with family, education, and determination...”可知，他主要想向怀揣远大梦想的年轻人传达关于追求大梦想的想法与信念。答案为A。

sections.title: 阅读理解 D
sections.instruction: 阅读下面语言材料，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。
sections.passage:
A bike-riding program for middle school students can help improve their mental (心理的) health, according to a new study from the Loma Linda University School of Medicine in California.

The program, called Riding for Focus (R4F), was organized by the nonprofit (非营利组织) Outride. Coaches spent six to eight weeks, at least three days a week, teaching middle school students cycling skills and riding outdoors with them. R4F hopes to improve the students' mental health and make them much happier.

For this study, Loma Linda University had students fill out surveys (调查) before and after the program to compare their mental condition. More than 800 students, from ages 11 to 14 and from 20 different schools, filled out the surveys.

The study found that there was a general increase in students' happiness after completing the cycling program. "We saw that there were mental health advantages across the whole population," Sean Wilson, a writer of the study, said in an interview. "More students had a 'positive (积极的) idea' on life."

"Middle school is an important time to pay attention to mental health because that's when many young people start to experience social pressure and stress from school," said Esther Walker, a program manager at Outride. Other research shows that one in five children deal with a mental, behavioral, or emotional illness. "The freedom and relief (轻松) that can come with going out for a bike ride could be helpful for students," Walker said.

questions.prompt: What can we know about R4F?
options: A. It was mainly for primary students.
B. It lasted eight weeks at most.
C. It was organized by a university.
D. It only allowed students to ride indoors.
questions.translation: 关于 R4F 我们能了解到什么？
questions.explanation: 根据第二段“Coaches spent six to eight weeks... teaching middle school students...”可知，该项目持续6到8周，因此最多持续8周（lasted eight weeks at most）。答案为B。

questions.prompt: Why were the students asked to fill out the before-and-after surveys?
options: A. To record their hobbies.
B. To record their physical condition.
C. To compare their change in their studies.
D. To compare their change in mental health.
questions.translation: 为什么要求学生在项目前后填写调查问卷？
questions.explanation: 根据第三段“Loma Linda University had students fill out surveys before and after the program to compare their mental condition.”可知，是为了比较他们心理健康状况的变化。答案为D。

questions.prompt: What does Paragraph 4 mainly talk about?
options: A. The steps of the study.
B. The results of the study.
C. Suggestions on riding bikes.
D. Ideas about the cycling program.
questions.translation: 第四段主要讲述了什么？
questions.explanation: 第四段开头写到“The study found that there was a general increase in students' happiness after completing the cycling program.”，展示了这项研究得出的结果。答案为B。

questions.prompt: Which of the following may Esther Walker agree with?
options: A. Most of the middle school students are in good mental health.
B. Primary school is the most important time for students.
C. Riding outdoors can improve students' mental health.
D. More students have a positive idea on life.
questions.translation: 埃斯瑟·沃克可能会同意以下哪项观点？
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段 Esther Walker 所说“The freedom and relief that can come with going out for a bike ride could be helpful for students”可知，她认为户外骑车有助于改善学生的心理健康。答案为C。

questions.prompt: What is the topic of the passage?
options: A. Life and health.
B. People and animals.
C. History and culture.
D. Nature and environment.
questions.translation: 这篇文章的主题是什么？
questions.explanation: 全篇围绕中学生骑车项目及其对心理健康的影响展开，属于生活与健康（Life and health）范畴。答案为A。

sections.title: 任务型阅读 E
sections.instruction: 根据短文内容完成任务。
sections.passage:
No matter how much research you do before a trip, you will experience some culture shock. So you should learn about the cultures of the place you want to visit.

If you have a tour abroad, for example, somewhere in Canada, it's better not to arrive early. However, in Austria, arriving on time is considered as a sign of respect (尊敬). And while tipping (给小费) is normal in the US, it isn't in a place like Slovenia. In Norway, you should never use your hands to eat, but a knife and a fork are not used when eating tacos in Mexico. Those are always eaten with your hands.

In fact, many of these international customs (习俗) are connected with food. In Egypt and Portugal, you should never ask for salt when having dinner. In Sierra Leone, you should always leave a small part of food when eating. Burping (打嗝) is socially acceptable in Iceland and Senegal, and in Japan making a sound while eating is a way of saying "thank you" for the meal.

The above offers a quick look at worldwide customs. However, wherever you go, you should always remember the customs accepted worldwide: avoid pointing with your finger, pay attention to everyone's time, and say hello to the old first.

questions.prompt: 1. 请将画线句子“So you should learn about the cultures of the place you want to visit.”译成汉语：
questions.answer: 所以你应该了解你想去游览的地方的文化。
questions.translation: 所以你应该了解你想去游览的地方的文化。
questions.explanation: So（所以），you should learn about（你应该了解），the cultures of the place（那个地方的文化），you want to visit（你想访问/游览的）。

questions.prompt: 2. 改为同义句：However, it is considered as a sign of respect _______________ on time in Austria.
questions.translation: 然而，在奥地利按时到达被视为一种尊重的标志。
questions.explanation: 原句为 'arriving on time is considered as a sign of respect in Austria.' 使用 it 作为形式主语时，真正的主语应用动词不定式 'to arrive'。

questions.prompt: 3. Can you eat tacos with a knife and a fork in Mexico?
questions.translation: 在墨西哥你能用刀叉吃塔可（墨西哥卷饼）吗？
questions.explanation: 根据第二段“a knife and a fork are not used when eating tacos in Mexico. Those are always eaten with your hands.”可知，不能用刀叉吃，必须用手吃，因此作否定回答：No, you can't.

questions.prompt: 4. What is allowed when you have dinner in Japan according to the passage?
questions.answer: Making a sound while eating is allowed.
questions.translation: 根据文章，在日本吃晚餐时什么是被允许的？
questions.explanation: 根据第三段最后“in Japan making a sound while eating is a way of saying 'thank you' for the meal.”可知，吃东西时发出声音是被允许且被视为感谢的方式。

questions.prompt: 5. How many customs does the writer mention in the last paragraph?
questions.translation: 作者在最后一段提到了几种习俗？
questions.explanation: 根据最后一段“avoid pointing with your finger, pay attention to everyone's time, and say hello to the old first.”可知，一共提到了3种全球通用的习俗。
